name: Gandrung

narrator.name: The Atlas narrator
narrator.voice: warm, unhurried, curious; a documentary voice that never oversells; speaks the dance's own words (names, counts) clearly
narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language
narrator.wardrobe: in each episode the narrator wears the traditional apparel associated with the dance, reconstructed with meticulous care from the profile's costume notes and the licensed images — genuine and respectful, never a caricature; sacred, ceremonial or restricted attire is never worn (the narrator stays in neutral dress with a respectful nod in colour and fabric); the pack's visual_brief.wardrobe says which
narrator.languages: master narration in English; translations per language in episodes/i18n/<lang>/<slug>.json with the same scene structure (pipeline/translate.py); names, places and counts are never translated

instructor.rule: counts out loud; demonstrates front and back; three slow repetitions before tempo; one correction at a time

scenes.title: Cold open
narration: The Dance of Love: Banyuwangi's Gandrung
This is Gandrung. Traditional.
on_screen: Hero video — MISSING
Title card: Gandrung · Indonesia · Traditional

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Originally a ritual dance dedicated to the goddess of rice and fertility, Dewi Sri, it is currently performed as a social dance of courtship and love in communal and social events, or as a tourist attraction.
on_screen: Map: Indonesia · Southeast Asia
Image 1 with attribution

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: It is performed as a social dance at communal and social events such as circumcisions or weddings, and as a tourist attraction.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage: UCLA Ethnomusicology Spring Festival of World Music 2025: Music of Java Ensemble (https://archive.org/details/calauem_200201_omvf0000672_pt1_ac)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dancer begins at the side of the stage, moves to the center with hip thrusts, and invites an audience member to dance by throwing a shawl to them.
Watch for Shawl Invitation.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: The dancer is dressed in traditional costume, with a fan, shawl, and ornamental headgear.
It is usually performed in an all-night performance that begins sometime around 9 p.m. and ends just before dawn.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Popular in Bali, Lombok, and Eastern Java; similar dances include ronggeng, tayuban, jaipongan, and joged.
on_screen: Names on screen as they are spoken
Variant names as a small list

scenes.title: Family tree
narration: Gandrung is similar of ronggeng: A similar dance known in East and Central Java.
Gandrung is similar of tayuban: A similar dance known in East and Central Java.
Gandrung is similar of jaipongan: A similar dance known in West Java and Banten.
Gandrung is similar of joged: A similar dance known in Jakarta.
